label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 17
knowledgePattern: Convert a ceiling-function integral into a finite geometric sum
solution:
For each integer j=1,2,…,99, the ceiling is j throughout (j−1,j]. Thus 2⌈x⌉ is constant at height 2j on an interval of width 1.

The isolated value at 0 has no effect on the integral. The required area is therefore ∑j=1992j=2(299−1)/(2−1)=2100−2. Answer F.

To check the endpoints, the first interval is (0,1] and the last is (98,99]; there are 99 rectangles.

hints.title: Read the supplied definition interval by interval
hints.body: List where the ceiling takes each successive integer value near the start of the integration range.
hints.recap: A piecewise definition can be analysed by cases, with its interval endpoints tracked explicitly.
hints.pitfall: The value at a single endpoint does not create an extra strip of area.
hints.pause: Describe the constant value of the integrand on each unit interval.

recall.reminder: A piecewise definition can be analysed by cases, with its interval endpoints tracked explicitly.

hints.title: Add the rectangular areas
hints.body: Each constant piece contributes its height times its width. Recognise the series formed by those contributions.
hints.recap: A finite GP is determined by its first term, common ratio and number of terms.
hints.pitfall: Count intervals rather than the number of integer labels visible at their endpoints.
hints.pause: Find those three quantities and calculate the total area.
